title: 56  Dark Matter
text:
56.5 The FTD Interpretation
In FTD, dark matter is not a new particle species: it is a property of the self-field halo surrounding every manifested particle.






WarningEpistemic Status



The self-field halo mechanism is [SELECTION] — physically motivated and supported by engine simulation evidence, but not rigorously proven from first principles. See DERIV_DARK_SECTOR_DYNAMICS.md for the full derivation and claims table.



56.5.1 Not New Particles, But Self-Field Tails
Every manifested particle (s = +/-1) in FTD continuously sources flux into its neighborhood via the coupling term. The resulting self-field envelope extends far beyond the particle itself:

r_eff (flux-weighted RMS radius): ~15 voxels
1% boundary: ~23 voxels (where flux falls to 1% of peak)
Self-field energy: 0.08 \(K_B^2\) per particle

These measurements come from GPU simulations at 128^3 lattice resolution (GP-KCOMP-SHELL test).


56.5.2 The Mechanism
Dark matter is the far-field tail of the self-field halo:
ORDINARY MATTER (the seed):
  Manifested particle (s = +/-1) at one lattice site
  Interacts via all forces (Coulomb, gravity, color)
  Emits/absorbs light

DARK MATTER (the halo):
  Self-field envelope (s = 0, |J| > 0) extending ~15-23 voxels
  Only gravitates (F = G_N * grad(rho), rho = |J|)
  No electromagnetic interaction (F_em = -alpha * s * grad(phi), s = 0)
The key insight: every particle carries its own dark matter halo. The self-field is gravitationally active but electromagnetically invisible because void sites (s = 0) do not couple to the Coulomb potential.

The FTD engine uses selective damping (default behavior): energy dissipation only occurs within 1 lattice hop of a manifested particle. Far-field flux — everything beyond the immediate particle neighborhood — propagates losslessly through the vacuum.

59.5 Black Hole Thermodynamics

59.5.1 Hawking Temperature
Stephen Hawking’s 1974 calculation (Hawking 1974) showed that black holes emit thermal radiation:
\[
T_H = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G M k_B} \approx 6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ K} \times \frac{M_\odot}{M}
\]
For stellar mass BH: Colder than CMB.


59.5.2 Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy
Jacob Bekenstein proposed (Bekenstein 1973) that black holes carry entropy proportional to horizon area:
\[
S = \frac{k_B c^3 A}{4 G \hbar}
\]
Entropy proportional to horizon area, not volume!


59.5.3 Hawking Radiation
Virtual pairs at horizon: - One particle falls in - One escapes - Black hole loses mass - Eventually evaporates
Timescale: \(t \propto M^3\)
For stellar BH: \(10^{67}\) years (far longer than universe age).

title: 59  Black Holes

59.6 The Information Paradox
If black holes evaporate via thermal radiation: - All information about what fell in is lost - Violates quantum mechanics (unitarity)
This is the famous information paradox: a conflict between quantum mechanics and general relativity.

59.6.1 The Problem Statement
When matter falls into a black hole and the black hole later evaporates, an apparent paradox emerges: the initial state is a pure quantum state |ψ⟩ with complete information, but the final state appears to be thermal radiation (a mixed state ρ) containing no memory of what fell in.






Figure 59.3: The information paradox and FTD resolution: information is preserved through flux tunneling at the stretched horizon.

title: 59  Black Holes
text:
59.7 The FTD Resolution
[CONJECTURE] In FTD, the information paradox may have a geometric resolution: information is preserved because the flux field evolution is unitary.

59.7.1 Flux Tunneling, Not Pair Production
The standard Hawking picture involves virtual pair production at the horizon: - One particle falls in, one escapes - The escaping particle is thermal (random)
FTD picture: Hawking radiation arises from flux tunneling. In the standard picture, virtual pairs form at the horizon with one falling in and one escaping as thermal radiation. In FTD, interior flux tunnels through the stretched horizon to become exterior flux, carrying information encoded in correlations. The flux field is continuous and does not have a sharp boundary at the horizon, allowing information encoded in flux correlations to tunnel out.


59.7.2 The Stretched Horizon
In FTD, the “horizon” is not a mathematical surface but a stretched horizon: a thin layer of highly scrambled flux:
\[\delta r \sim \ell_P \sqrt{\frac{M}{M_P}}\]
This layer: - Scrambles infalling information rapidly (thermalization time ~ M log M) - Preserves information in flux correlations - Gradually releases it through tunneling


59.7.3 The Page Curve
The Page curve describes how entanglement entropy of radiation changes as the black hole evaporates:






Figure 59.4: The Page curve showing entanglement entropy evolution during black hole evaporation.



Key features: - Entropy increases during first half (information going in) - Entropy decreases during second half (information coming out) - Returns to zero (unitarity preserved)
[SELECTION] FTD’s action principle implies unitary flux evolution (see THEORETICAL_FOUNDATIONS Part II for the argument). The Page curve follows automatically.






ImportantNo Information Loss



In FTD, the flux field’s unitary evolution guarantees information preservation. The “paradox” arises only if you treat the horizon as a sharp classical boundary: but it is not.




59.7.4 No Firewall Needed
The “firewall paradox” arises from trying to preserve unitarity while maintaining a smooth horizon. The proposed solution (firewall) would make the horizon violent for infalling observers.
FTD avoids this: - The stretched horizon scrambles information - No need for drama at the horizon - Infalling observer experiences nothing special (until tidal forces) - Information escapes via continuous flux tunneling


59.7.5 The Holographic Bound
The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy:
\[S = \frac{A}{4\ell_P^2}\]
In FTD, this reflects the number of independent flux modes on the stretched horizon:
\[N_{\text{modes}} = \frac{A}{\ell_P^2}\]
The factor of 4 arises from the Hilbert space structure: each mode has 2 polarizations and 2 helicities.


59.7.6 What Happens to Infalling Information?

Falls in: Information encoded in manifested particles
Scrambles: Rapidly thermalized at stretched horizon (time ~ M log M)
Correlates: Encoded in subtle correlations of flux field
Tunnels out: Gradually escapes via Hawking radiation
Reconstructed: In principle, pure state recoverable from complete radiation

The entire process is unitary. [CONJECTURE] Information may be preserved through this mechanism.

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.1 The Gap We Must Bridge
“What is it to be alive, precisely?”
FTD derives physics from the lattice up: - Particles from manifestation - Atoms from binding - Molecules from chemistry - Materials from aggregation
But somewhere in this hierarchy, life appears. What distinguishes: - A rock (not alive) from a bacterium (alive)? - A dead cell from a living cell? - A complex machine from an organism?
We need a definition that is: 1. Precise: Stated in FTD terms 2. Operational: Decidable in principle 3. Non-arbitrary: Captures what we mean by “life”

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.2 What Life Is Not

63.2.1 Not Complexity Alone
A hurricane is complex: it has structure, dynamics, and information flow. But a hurricane is not alive. Complexity is necessary but not sufficient.


63.2.2 Not Self-Replication Alone
Fire spreads and “reproduces.” Crystals grow. Prions copy themselves. But none of these are alive in the full sense. Replication is necessary but not sufficient.


63.2.3 Not Carbon-Based
This is chemistry-dependent, not fundamental. Silicon life, if it exists, would still be life.


63.2.4 Not “Has DNA”
DNA is one implementation of genetic memory. It is not the definition.

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.3 The FTD Definition of Life






ImportantDefinition: Life



A living system is a spatially localized pattern of manifested states \(\{s(v)\}\) that:

Maintains organization against entropy by continuous flux exchange with environment
Contains a self-model (representation of its own structure encoded in its configuration)
Uses the self-model to guide behavior (feedback loop that references the model)
Propagates the pattern (creates copies or successors that inherit the self-model)



Let us examine each criterion.

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.4 Criterion 1: Maintenance Against Entropy

63.4.1 The Second Law
Isolated systems evolve toward maximum entropy. Structure dissipates. Order degrades.


63.4.2 The Living Exception
Living systems locally decrease entropy by: - Importing low-entropy energy (food, sunlight) - Exporting high-entropy waste (heat, CO2) - Using the difference to maintain structure
In FTD terms: \[\frac{d S_{\text{local}}}{dt} < 0 \quad \text{while} \quad \frac{d S_{\text{total}}}{dt} > 0\]
The organism stays ordered; the universe becomes more disordered overall.


63.4.3 Operational Test
A system satisfies Criterion 1 if: - Cut off from flux exchange, it degrades (death) - With flux exchange, it maintains structure indefinitely
A rock fails: it does not need flux exchange to persist. A fire fails: it does not maintain a specific structure. A cell passes: cut off from nutrients, it dies; with nutrients, it maintains.

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.5 Criterion 2: Self-Model

63.5.1 What Is a Self-Model?
A self-model is a configuration within the system that represents the system’s structure:
\[\phi: \Omega \to \mathcal{M}\]
where: - \(\Omega\) is the system’s physical substrate - \(\mathcal{M}\) is the representation space - \(\phi\) encodes information about \(\Omega\)’s structure

In FTD terms: a pattern of states that, when “read” by the system’s dynamics, produces a copy of that pattern along with the rest of the organism.

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.6 Criterion 3: Feedback from Self-Model

63.6.1 Model-Guided Behavior
Having a self-model is not enough. The system must use the model:
\[\text{Action}(t+1) = f(\text{State}(t), \phi(\Omega))\]
Behavior depends on both current state AND the self-model.

63.6.3 Why This Matters
A crystal has structure but no self-model. A computer has data about itself but does not use it to maintain itself (unless programmed to). Life uses its self-model for self-maintenance.

title: 63  The Definition of Life

63.7 Criterion 4: Pattern Propagation

63.7.1 Inheritance
Living systems produce successors that: - Have similar structure (inheritance) - Contain the self-model (or a copy) - Can themselves satisfy Criteria 1-3


63.7.2 Variation
Copies need not be exact. Mutation, variation, and evolution are permitted. What matters is: - The self-model is transmitted - Successors can be living systems

title: 63  The Definition of Life

63.8 The Formal Definition
Putting it together:






ImportantDefinition (Formal)



A configuration \(\Omega \subset \mathcal{L}\) is living at time \(t\) if:

\(\exists\) continuous flux exchange \(\mathbf{J}_{\text{in}}, \mathbf{J}_{\text{out}}\) maintaining \(S(\Omega) < S_{\text{max}}\)

Under favorable conditions, \(\Omega\) produces \(\Omega'\) with \(\phi' \approx \phi\) (propagation)

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:
63.9 The Void Cycle of Life
Life follows the pattern:
\[0 \xrightarrow{\text{genesis}} \pm 1 \xrightarrow{\text{maintenance}} \pm 1 \xrightarrow{\text{death}} 0\]
More specifically:
BIRTH:    Flux concentrates → Manifestation → Organization
LIFE:     Flux exchange → Self-maintenance → Self-replication
DEATH:    Flux disperses → Structure degrades → Return to void
Every living thing is a temporary excursion from void, sustained by flux, and destined to return.

In FTD terms: 1. Complex chemistry creates autocatalytic cycles (Criterion 1 precursor) 2. Information-bearing polymers emerge (Criterion 2 precursor) 3. Coupling between catalysis and information creates feedback (Criterion 3) 4. Template replication enables propagation (Criterion 4)

title: 63  The Definition of Life
text:

These are patterns of behavior among living things, not living things themselves. They lack: - Physical substrate undergoing flux exchange - Continuous maintenance against entropy at the pattern level


63.12.2 Excluded: AI (Currently)
Current AI systems: - Have no physical self-model (their code is not “about” their hardware) - Do not maintain themselves against entropy - Do not propagate copies that inherit the self-model
This could change with different architectures.


63.12.3 Included: Hypothetical Silicon Life
If a silicon-based system satisfied all four criteria, it would be alive by this definition.

63.14 Transition
With life defined in FTD terms, we can now examine how living systems self-organize, how they encode and process information, and how consciousness emerges from sufficiently complex life (see Ch. 21 for the formal treatment). title: 64  Self-Organization

64.1 Patterns from Simple Rules
“Order from chaos”

title: 64  Self-Organization
text:
64.1.1 The Surprise of Emergence
When you follow simple rules: - No individual knows the pattern - No central control exists - Yet structure appears
This is self-organization.


64.1.2 Cellular Automata
Local rules → global patterns.

64.1.2.1 Conway’s Game of Life
Four simple rules govern each cell’s fate:

Underpopulation: fewer than 2 neighbors causes death
Survival: 2-3 neighbors allows survival
Overpopulation: more than 3 neighbors causes death
Reproduction: exactly 3 neighbors triggers birth

From four rules: gliders, oscillators, and Turing-complete computation.






Figure 64.1: Examples of self-organization from simple rules: cellular automata patterns, convection cells, and other emergent structures.






64.1.3 Reaction-Diffusion
Turing patterns from activator-inhibitor dynamics: \[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = D_u \nabla^2 u + f(u,v)
\] \[
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} = D_v \nabla^2 v + g(u,v)
\]
Creates spots, stripes, spirals: the patterns of life.


64.1.4 Flocking (Boids)
Reynolds’ three rules: 1. Separation: Avoid crowding neighbors 2. Alignment: Match heading with neighbors 3. Cohesion: Move toward average position
Result: Emergent flocking behavior indistinguishable from birds.

64.2.4 Hurricanes

64.8 Transition
Order emerges from chaos. But what is order, really? What distinguishes organized from disorganized? Next (Chapter 66), we explore information and entropy: the deep mathematical structures that quantify organization.
FTD itself exemplifies self-organization: from the simplest possible rules (local updates on a ternary lattice), the entire complexity of the universe emerges without top-down design. 66.3 Von Neumann Entropy

66.3.1 Quantum Information
For quantum systems, Shannon entropy is insufficient. We need the von Neumann entropy: \[
S_{vN} = -\text{Tr}(\rho \ln \rho)
\]
where \(\rho\) is the density matrix describing the quantum state.


66.3.2 Density Matrix in FTD
In the FTD Hilbert space H_TRD = L²(Lattice, ℂ), the density matrix for a pure state |ψ⟩ is: \[
\rho = |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|
\]
For mixed states (statistical ensembles of pure states): \[
\rho = \sum_i p_i |\psi_i\rangle\langle\psi_i|
\]

66.3.4 Entanglement Entropy
For entangled systems A ⊗ B, the entanglement entropy measures quantum correlations: \[
S_A = -\text{Tr}(\rho_A \ln \rho_A)
\]
where \(\rho_A = \text{Tr}_B(\rho_{AB})\) is the reduced density matrix.






NoteFTD Connection



In FTD, entangled pairs created via pair production have: - Pure total state: S_vN(AB) = 0 - Mixed subsystems: S_vN(A) = S_vN(B) = ln(2)
This matches the quantum prediction for maximally entangled Bell states.




66.3.5 Area Law
For ground states of local Hamiltonians, entanglement entropy scales with boundary area: \[
S_A \propto \frac{\text{Area}(\partial A)}{l_P^2}
\]
This connects to the holographic principle and black hole entropy.

title: 66  Information and Entropy
text:
66.4 The Connection

66.4.1 Landauer’s Principle
Erasing one bit of information: \[
E_{min} = k_B T \ln(2)
\]
At room temperature: ~\(3 \times 10^{-21}\) J per bit.
Information is physical. Computation has thermodynamic cost.


66.4.2 Maxwell’s Demon (Standard Resolution)






Figure 66.1: Maxwell’s demon attempts to sort fast and slow molecules, but the second law is preserved because storing and erasing information about each molecule requires entropy production.



The resolution: the demon must store information about each molecule’s velocity, and erasing that information (Landauer’s principle) costs entropy. The second law remains inviolate.

title: 66  Information and Entropy
text:
66.5 The Second Law

66.5.1 Statement
Total entropy of isolated system never decreases: \[
dS_{total} \geq 0
\]


66.5.2 Why?
Not a fundamental law: a statistical truth: - Overwhelmingly more disordered states than ordered - Random evolution → most likely state - Most likely = highest entropy

66.6.2 The Past Hypothesis
Universe started in extraordinarily low entropy state: - Big Bang: Smooth, uniform - Today: Clumpy, complex - Heat death: Smooth again


66.6.3 In FTD Terms
The universe begins in the all-Void state (s = 0 everywhere), the minimum entropy configuration. As time progresses, genesis creates particles that clump and form structures, increasing local complexity while global entropy rises. Eventually the universe returns toward void, approaching maximum entropy in the heat death.


66.6.4 The Boundary Condition Solution
Why did the universe start with low entropy? In FTD, the answer is boundary conditions on the action principle.
The FTD action:
\[S[s,J] = \sum_t \sum_v \mathcal{L}(s,J)\]
requires boundary conditions at both temporal ends. Variational principles need to know where to start and where to end.
Initial condition: The simplest boundary is all-Void:
\[s(v, t=0) = 0 \quad \forall v\]
This is the unique maximum-symmetry state: homogeneous, isotropic, zero information content.
Final condition: The action principle requires specifying the endpoint. In cosmology, this is the heat death state:
\[\lim_{t \to \infty} S(t) = S_{max}\]
Maximum entropy, uniform distribution, no gradients.






ImportantThe Arrow is Geometric



The arrow of time is not a mystery to be explained: it is a boundary condition of the variational problem. Time’s direction is the direction from low-entropy boundary to high-entropy boundary.




66.6.5 Why This Boundary?
Why these particular boundary conditions? Three answers:

Anthropic: Only universes with low initial entropy produce observers. We could not be asking this question otherwise.
Uniqueness: The all-Void state is the unique state with maximum symmetry. Any other initial condition requires specifying additional structure: breaking symmetry without explanation.
Self-consistency: The action principle itself requires smooth boundaries. The all-Void → heat-death trajectory is the smoothest possible evolution.



66.6.6 Retrocausality and the Block Universe
In FTD, the action principle is non-local in time. The path that extremizes S depends on both initial and final conditions.
This does not mean the future causes the past. It means:



View
Interpretation

Universe evolves tick-by-tick, following rules


Block
Entire 4D history extremizes action



Both views are valid. The rules are local; the explanation is global.


66.6.7 Information is Conserved
The flux field evolution is unitary: information is never created or destroyed, only redistributed.
\[I_{total}(t) = I_{total}(0) = \text{constant}\]
Entropy increases because information spreads out, not because it disappears. The distinction matters for:

Black hole information paradox: Information escapes via Hawking radiation correlations
Quantum mechanics: Unitarity preserved at the fundamental level
Reversibility: In principle, the simulation could run backward

def compute_entropy(grid):
    # Partition into cells
    cells = partition(grid, CELL_SIZE)

    # Count particles per cell
    counts = [len(c.particles) for c in cells]

    # Compute probability distribution
    total = sum(counts)
    probs = [c/total for c in counts if c > 0]

    # Shannon entropy
    H = -sum(p * log2(p) for p in probs)

    return H

67.5.1 The Mandelbrot Boundary as Edge of Chaos
The Mandelbrot set provides the clearest visualization of the edge of chaos:

Inside the set (ordered): Orbits converge to fixed points or cycles. Predictable, stable, but computationally trivial.
Outside the set (chaotic): Orbits escape to infinity. No structure, no memory, no computation.
At the boundary (critical): Orbits neither converge nor escape. This is where all the complexity lives.

The entire infinitely complex fractal boundary is the edge between order and chaos. This is not coincidence. The boundary is exactly where the iteration is “deciding” whether to persist or dissolve, whether to remain bounded or escape.
This is the locus of consciousness: not in the stable interior (unconscious automation) nor in the chaotic exterior (no coherent process) but at the critical boundary where the sLoop perpetually balances between persistence and dissolution.

70.2 The Big Crunch

70.2.1 Gravity Wins
If dark energy weakens or reverses: - Expansion slows - Stops - Reverses


70.2.2 The Collapse
The universe expands to a maximum size, then begins contracting. As it contracts, structures merge, temperature rises, all matter becomes compressed, and eventually reaches a singularity: the Big Crunch, a time-reversal of the Big Bang.


70.2.3 The Final Moments
As universe contracts: - CMB blueshifts, heats - Stars cooked by radiation - Nuclei dissociate - Quark-gluon plasma - Final singularity
Time reversal of Big Bang.

Perhaps the universe cycles: - Contracts to minimum - Bounces - Expands again - Repeat forever


70.3.2 Cyclic Cosmology

70.4.2 Isolation
Eventually: - Galaxies beyond horizon - Observable universe: Just our local group - Then just our galaxy remnant - Then just scattered particles


70.4.3 Effective Heat Death
Same endpoint as heat death, but: - Faster approach - More isolated - More expansion

title: 70  Alternative Endings

70.5 Vacuum Decay

70.5.1 The False Vacuum
Our vacuum might not be ground state: - Metastable configuration - Could decay to true vacuum


70.5.2 The Bubble of Death
A true vacuum bubble nucleates at some random point in spacetime, then expands outward at nearly the speed of light. Everything inside the bubble has different physics, different constants, different particles. There is no warning and no escape.


70.5.3 Consequences
Inside true vacuum: - Different physics - Different constants - Different particles - No chemistry, no life


70.5.4 Probability
Tunneling probability per unit volume: \[
P \propto e^{-S}
\]
Very small, but not zero.
Could happen anytime, anywhere.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.2 A

Accretion

The accumulation of matter by gravitational attraction. In FTD, particles clump when density gradients exert net force toward centers.

Annihilation

The collision of matter (+1) and antimatter (-1) particles, both returning to void (0) and releasing their energy as flux waves.

Anthropic Principle

The observation that the universe’s constants must permit observers, since we exist to observe them.

Antimatter

State -1 particles. Equivalent to matter in all ways except opposite charge/polarity. Annihilates with matter upon contact.

Alpha Power Ladder

The hierarchical sequence of α powers encoding fundamental mass and energy scales: α⁸ (Higgs VEV), α¹¹ (electron mass), α¹⁶ (vacuum energy), α²⁰ (gravitational coupling). The gaps {3, 5, 4} between exponents encode framework integers.

Alpha Precision Formula

The correction formula achieving 0.21 ppt accuracy for \(\alpha\): \(1/\alpha = x_+ - (9/47)|\varepsilon| + (5/64)|\varepsilon|^2\) where \(\varepsilon = e^\pi - \pi - 20 \approx -9 \times 10^{-4}\). The correction term 9/47 combines framework integers (47 = N_c × N_base² - 1 = 3×16-1), and remarkably |ε| ≈ 1/1111 where 1111 = (b₃+N_base)(8N_eff-N_c) = 11×101. The constant 20 = b₃ + N_eff = 7 + 13 = 1/c_fermion connects to the Weyl anomaly coefficient from conformal field theory. This 6,000× improvement over the base 1.26 ppm derivation represents the most precise theoretical prediction of α ever achieved.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.3 B

b₃ (QCD Beta Coefficient)

Framework integer = 7. The first coefficient in the QCD beta function for SU(3). Appears in electron mass (70 = \(b_3(b_3+N_c)\)) and gravitational coupling (\(1/(b_3+N_c)^2\)).

Born Rule (as Translation Protocol)

The interpretation of the Born rule P = |ψ|² not as a mysterious postulate but as the translation protocol between Domain A (configurations) and Domain B (probabilities). The squared amplitude is what remains invariant under domain crossing.

Bridge Operator (𝒯)

The mathematical structure that translates between Domain A (ontic/classical) and Domain B (epistemic/probabilistic). In quantum mechanics, the Born rule P = |ψ|² serves as the bridge operator. See also: Domain A, Domain B.

Baryon

A composite particle made of three quarks (triad configuration). Includes protons and neutrons.

Bell Test

Experimental verification of quantum correlations exceeding classical bounds. Measures S parameter (classical ≤2, quantum ≤2√2).

Big Bang

The initial genesis event from which the universe emerged. In FTD, initial flux creates conditions for widespread particle genesis.

Binding

The locking of particles into stable structures (triads, shells). Bound particles resist decay.

Bounded Orbit (Mandelbrot)

An orbit in the Mandelbrot iteration that remains finite forever. Points with bounded orbits lie inside the set. In FTD, analogous to conscious processes that sustain themselves indefinitely - the iteration keeps going.

Black Hole

A region where density is so high that the escape velocity exceeds C. Particles entering cannot leave.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.4 C

C (Speed of Causality)

Fundamental constant = 1.0 voxel/tick. The maximum speed at which any influence can propagate. Nothing exceeds C.

Casimir Effect

Attractive force between close surfaces due to excluded vacuum fluctuation modes. Demonstrates reality of zero-point energy.

Ce₂Zr₂O₇ (Cerium Zirconium Oxide)

Pyrochlore material exhibiting quantum spin ice behavior. In 2025, confirmed as the first material showing emergent photon-like excitations from discrete lattice dynamics, validating FTD’s core mechanism of gauge boson emergence from constraint structure.

CP Violation (in Baryons)

Asymmetry between matter and antimatter decay rates in three-quark systems. First observed in baryons by LHCb in 2025 (Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻, 5.2σ). FTD derives CP violation from integer ratios: δ_CP = arctan(7/3) ≈ 66.8°.

Calorimeter

Detector measuring particle energy by total absorption. Used in particle physics experiments.

Cantor Dust (Julia Set)

The Julia set for parameters c outside the Mandelbrot set. A totally disconnected set of points: the “dust” that remains when bounded orbits become infinitely rare. In FTD, the consciousness regime (k = 0.5, c ≈ 0.676) produces Cantor dust Julia sets, representing the open, indeterminate nature of conscious dynamics.

Consciousness Quadratic

The master quadratic evaluated at k = 0.5 (consciousness regime): y² - (G)²y/2 + (G)³/2 = 0. Yields complex roots y = 2.19 ± 2.86i, placing consciousness outside the Mandelbrot set in a fundamentally different ontological regime from physics (which has real roots).

Consciousness Regime

The parameter region k = 0.5 in the TRD-Mandelbrot framework. Characterized by: Mandelbrot parameter c ≈ 0.676 (outside the set), complex quadratic roots, escaping orbits, Cantor dust Julia sets, and open/indeterminate dynamics. Contrasts with the physics regime (k = 16, inside the set, real roots, bounded orbits).

Critical Coefficient (k_c)

The value k_c = 4/G* ≈ 1.352 at which the TRD-Mandelbrot transformation maps to the cardioid cusp c = 1/4. The boundary between bounded and unbounded regimes. Satisfies the exact identity k_c × c_cusp × G* = 1.

Chain of Necessity

The dependency chain used in this book to organize which results rely on which inputs. Where the text asserts “uniqueness,” it is always meant relative to an explicitly stated constraint class or search space (see the Assumption Ledger).

Charge

A property that determines electromagnetic interaction. In FTD, derived from quark composition (±1/3, ±2/3).

Complexity

Properties of wholes that emerge from but are not present in parts. Arises from interactions between many components.

Conformal Anomaly (c_fermion)

The trace anomaly coefficient in conformal field theory for a Weyl fermion: c_fermion = 1/20. In FTD, the reciprocal 20 = b₃ + N_eff = 7 + 13 appears in the alpha precision formula as the constant in ε = e^π - π - 20. This remarkable connection between framework integers and CFT provides independent theoretical support for the precision formula.

Curl

Vector differential operator measuring rotation in a field. Used for magnetic force calculations.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.5 D

Distinction

The primitive epistemic act of marking one thing as different from another. In EPL-ST, distinction is the absolute foundation from which all else follows, prior to logic, truth, or existence. The ability to distinguish “this” from “that” is the most basic operation of any epistemic agent. From distinction alone, the ternary valuation {+1, −1, 0} follows as a theorem. See ?sec-formal-logic.

Dark Energy

The component driving accelerating expansion. In FTD, emergent from dynamic void flux: ρ_DE = ½⟨J²⟩_vacuum. DESI 2025 data (4.2σ) shows w evolves over cosmic time, consistent with FTD prediction that void flux is dynamic, not constant.

Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI)

Spectroscopic survey instrument at Kitt Peak National Observatory. DR2 (2025) provided 4.2σ evidence for evolving dark energy (w₀ ≈ −0.7, wₐ ≈ −1), challenging the cosmological constant and supporting FTD’s dynamic void interpretation.

Dispositional Ontology

The philosophical position that reality is fundamentally composed of dispositions (tendencies, potentials) rather than categorical properties. In FTD, the flux field J represents dispositional properties of the void substrate.

Domain A (𝒜)

The ontic/classical domain of configurations. Contains definite states, actual arrangements, and physical structures. Distinguished from Domain B by containing no probabilities, only actualities. The substrate of what is.

Domain B (ℬ)

The epistemic/probabilistic domain. Contains probability distributions, knowledge states, and information about systems. Distinguished from Domain A by containing no definite configurations, only distributions over possibilities. The domain of what is known or knowable.

Domain Confusion

The philosophical error of projecting properties appropriate to one domain onto another. Examples include treating probabilities as physical substances (B→A error) or treating configurations as merely epistemic (A→B error).

Domain Interpenetration

The property that Domain A and Domain B exist within each other: physical structures in A can encode information (B content), while probability distributions in B describe configurations in A. Neither domain is more fundamental.

Dark Matter

Non-luminous matter detected only by gravitational effects. In FTD, potentially particles that interact gravitationally but not electromagnetically.

Decay

The gradual reduction of flux magnitude. Controlled by DECAY_RATE. Bound particles have suppressed decay.

Density

The magnitude of the flux vector: ρ = |J|. Determines genesis probability when above KB.

Divergence

Scalar field measuring flux source/sink at a point. Positive divergence → matter genesis; negative → antimatter.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.6 E

Electromagnetism

Force between charged particles. Arises from charge gradients in FTD.

EPL-ST (Epistemic-Physical Logic with Sorts and Times)

The formal logical framework underlying FTD. Establishes six primitive sorts (Observers, Epistemic States, Propositions, Distinctions, Events, Worlds), proves ternary valuation is necessary, and derives the requirement for 3D space from stable embedding conditions. See ?sec-formal-logic.

Epistemic Extension

A mapping φ: E → E′ where new distinctions may be added while preserving all prior distinctions consistently. The requirement that epistemic extension be stable leads to the theorem that d ≥ 3 dimensions are necessary.

Electron Electric Dipole Moment (eEDM)

A measure of the asymmetric charge distribution along the electron’s spin axis. A non-zero eEDM would indicate CP violation beyond the Standard Model. The 2025 JILA measurement set the world’s best limit: |d_e| < 4.1 × 10⁻³⁰ e·cm. FTD predicts d_e ≈ 0 for fundamental manifestations, consistent with observation.

Encoding Relation

The mathematical map ε: A → B that extracts epistemic content (information, meaning) from physical structure. A book encodes information; a brain encodes beliefs. The encoding relation is how Domain A structures can “contain” Domain B content.

Epistemic Inertia

Resistance to belief change proportional to the “mass” of evidence supporting current beliefs. Analogous to physical inertia but in Domain B. See also: Noetic Mass.

Epistemic Physical Object

A configuration in Domain A that encodes content from Domain B. Examples: books (encode information), brains (encode beliefs), measurement devices (encode measurement results). The mechanism by which domains interpenetrate.

Edge of Chaos

The critical boundary between ordered (predictable) and chaotic (random) regimes where maximum computational capability exists. Visualized perfectly by the Mandelbrot set boundary: inside is order, outside is chaos, the boundary itself is where all complexity lives. In FTD, the locus of consciousness.

Eight Thousand One Hundred Twenty-Eight (8128 = T(127))

The 127th triangular number. Remarkably, 8128 is the fourth perfect number (equals the sum of its proper divisors: 1+2+4+…+4064 = 8128). Appears in bottom quark mass: m_b/m_e = T(127) + 42 = 8128 + 42 = 8170.

Eight Thousand One Hundred Seventy (8170)

Bottom/electron mass ratio = T(127) + 42 = 8128 + 42 = 8170. Combines the perfect number 8128 with the bridge constant 42. Error: 0.12%.

Eleven Hundred Eleven (1111)

The quantum correction denominator in the alpha precision formula: 1111 = 11 × 101 = (b₃ + N_base)(8N_eff - N_c) = (7+4)(8×13-3) = 11 × 101. Remarkably, |ε| = |e^π - π - 20| ≈ 1/1111 to high precision. All four framework integers {3, 4, 7, 13} participate in this single number, suggesting it represents a fundamental coupling constant. The factorization into twin primes 11 and 101 may have deeper significance.

Emergence

The appearance of novel properties at higher levels of organization. Atoms have wetness; electrons do not.

Emergent Gauge Bosons

Gauge field quanta (photon-like excitations) that arise from collective dynamics of an underlying discrete system rather than being fundamental. Confirmed in quantum spin ice (Ce₂Zr₂O₇, 2025), validating FTD’s core mechanism where photons emerge from flux field dynamics on a lattice.

Entanglement

Correlation between particles created together (pair production). Shared UUID indicates common origin.

Entropy

Measure of disorder or uncertainty. Always increases in isolated systems (Second Law).

Eight (8 = 2^N_c)

Derived integer = 2³. Appears as the denominator in the W boson mass formula (8α²) where it encodes SU(2) weak isospin structure. Also equals Fibonacci F₆.

Escaping Orbit (Mandelbrot)

An orbit in the Mandelbrot iteration that diverges to infinity. Points with escaping orbits lie outside the set. In FTD, analogous to processes that cannot sustain themselves - the iteration stops, returning to void.

Evaporation

Transition from manifested state (±1) to void (0) when density drops below KB.

Event Horizon

Boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.7 F

Fibonacci Skeleton

The underlying structure of FTD’s framework integers as Fibonacci numbers. F₄=3=N_c, F₆=8=2^N_c, F₇=13=N_eff, F₁₀=55=T(10). The effective dimension equals the Fibonacci of the loop length: N_eff = F(b₃).

Fifty-Five (55 = T(10))

The tenth triangular number = 10 × 11/2 = 55. Also Fibonacci F₁₀. Appears in the proton mass formula: m_p/m_e = N_eff/α + T(b₃ + N_c) = 13 × 137 + 55 ≈ 1836.

Fine Structure Constant (α)

Dimensionless constant = 1/137.036 (0.007297). DERIVED from the master quadratic as the larger root. Controls electromagnetic strength. Base accuracy: 1.26 ppm; Precision formula: 0.21 ppt (6,000× better) via 1/α = x₊ - (9/47)|ε| + (5/64)|ε|² where ε = e^π - π - 20 ≈ -9×10⁻⁴. See also: Alpha Precision Formula.

Flux

3D vector field J = [Jx, Jy, Jz] representing momentum/energy. The substrate of potential.

Four Framework Integers

The minimal inputs {b₃=7, N_c=3, N_eff=13, N_base=4} from which all constants are derived. See individual entries.

Force

Influence that changes particle momentum. Four forces: gravity, electromagnetic, strong, weak.

Frequency

Rate of oscillation. Related to energy by E = hf.

Forty-One (41 = N_eff × N_c + 2)

Derived integer = 13 × 3 + 2 = 41. The ratio between top and bottom quark masses: m_t/m_b = 41. Notably, 41 = 42 - 1, connecting the top quark to the bridge constant minus unity. A prime number.

Forty-Two (42 = 2 × N_c × b₃)

The bridge constant = 2 × 3 × 7 = 42. Equals the product of the first four Heegner numbers (1 × 2 × 3 × 7). Appears as the additive correction in tau mass (3477 = 17 × 207 - 42) and bottom quark mass (8170 = T(127) + 42). The prime counting function π(42) = 13 = N_eff, creating a remarkable number-theoretic closure.

Forty-Seven (47 = N_c × N_base² - 1)

Derived integer = 3 × 16 - 1 = 47. Appears as the denominator in the alpha precision formula: the correction term 9/47 provides the first-order improvement from 1.26 ppm to sub-ppm accuracy. A prime number.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.8 G

Genesis

Transition from void (0) to manifested state (±1). Occurs probabilistically when density exceeds KB.

Graded Monism

The ontological position that reality consists of one fundamental substance (the void) with multiple modes or grades of being. Distinguished from dualism (two substances) and eliminative monism (only one mode). In FTD: void (substrate) → flux (disposition) → manifestation (actuality).

Gradient

Vector pointing in direction of maximum increase. Gradients drive forces.

Global(t)

Everything at one tick. The complete state of the universe at timestamp \(t\). Contains all entities, observers, and configurations.

Gravity

Force proportional to density gradient. Always attractive. Weakest force but infinite range.

Gravitational Wave Detector

Instrument (e.g., LIGO, Virgo) detecting spacetime ripples from massive object mergers via laser interferometry.

GZK Cutoff

Maximum energy for cosmic rays, limited by interaction with CMB photons.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.9 H

Hadron Collider

Accelerator colliding protons or heavy ions at high energies. LHC at CERN reaches 13 TeV center-of-mass energy.

H (Planck Resolution)

Fundamental constant = 1.0. The quantum of action. Corresponds to ℏ.

H(Ω,t) (Horizon)

What observer Ω can perceive at tick \(t\). A subset of Global(t). Mediated by six senses: sight, sound, touch, taste, smell, cognition.

Hadron

Particle made of quarks. Baryons (3 quarks) or mesons (quark-antiquark pair).

Hawking Radiation

Thermal radiation from black holes due to virtual pair production at horizon.

Heat Death

Final state of universe with maximum entropy. All gradients eliminated.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.10 I

Interference

Combination of flux waves. Constructive when aligned; destructive when opposed.

Ionization

Removal of electron from atom. Creates charged ion.

is_locked

Boolean flag indicating particle is part of stable structure. Locked particles resist decay.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.11 J

j-Invariant (1728 = 12³)

The modular j-invariant = 12³ = (N_base × N_c)³ = (4 × 3)³ = 1728. This value is derived from framework integers, not selected. The j-invariant determines the complex multiplication structure of elliptic curves; j = 1728 corresponds to the curve y² = x³ - x with complex multiplication by i. This special curve underlies the master quadratic derivation of α.

Jeans Mass

Minimum mass for gravitational collapse to overcome pressure.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.12 K

KB (Existence Threshold)

Fundamental constant = 0.511. Minimum density for manifestation. Corresponds to electron mass-energy.

Kerr Black Hole

Rotating black hole with ergosphere and ring singularity.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.13 L

Laplacian

Second-order differential operator. Measures deviation from neighborhood average.

Lemniscate-Alpha Curve

The self-referential harmonic curve used to construct a geometric route to the master quadratic. Its arc length reproduces α = 1/137.036 with 1.26 ppm accuracy under the stated construction. Claims of “uniqueness” are to be read as uniqueness within the stated constraint set.

**Lemniscatic Constant (G*)**

The lemniscatic constant used in this book, \(G^*\approx 2.9587\) (not to be confused with Gauss’s classical constant \(\varpi\approx 2.622\)). Appears in the master quadratic relating the electromagnetic root and the color root. Additional algebraic identities (e.g., in terms of the quadratic roots) are recorded where used.

Lepton

Fundamental particle (electron, muon, tau, neutrinos). Not made of quarks.

Loop Self-Enumeration

The property that b₃ = N_base + N_c = 4 + 3 = 7. The FTD loop length equals the sum of its structural parameters: the framework counts itself.

Lorentz Force

Magnetic force on moving charges. Perpendicular to both velocity and field.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.14 M

Mandelbrot Set

The set of complex numbers c for which the iteration z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c remains bounded. A mathematical archetype of self-reference where output becomes input. In FTD, serves as a visual and conceptual analog for the sLoop: bounded orbits correspond to persistent consciousness, escaping orbits correspond to return to void, and the infinitely complex boundary represents the edge of consciousness where all complexity lives.

Mandelbrot Boundary

The infinitely detailed edge between the Mandelbrot set’s interior (bounded orbits) and exterior (escaping orbits). This boundary, where the iteration is perpetually “deciding” whether to persist or dissolve, serves as the mathematical portrait of the edge of chaos and the locus of consciousness in FTD.

Mandelbrot-Lemniscate Bridge

The exact mathematical identity k_c × c_cusp × G* = 1 connecting TRD parameter space to the Mandelbrot set. The transformation c = 1/(k × G*) maps TRD coefficient k to Mandelbrot parameter c. Physics (k=16) maps inside the set; consciousness (k=0.5) maps outside.

Minimum Distance (d_min)

The irreducible gap d_min = (G*)²/32 ≈ 0.2736 that the Lemniscate-Alpha curve maintains from the origin. Represents the threshold requirement for manifestation: physics cannot emerge directly from pure void. The divisor 32 = k_physics/k_consciousness = 16/0.5 is the regime ratio.

Manifestation

The realized state (±1). Distinguished from potential (flux in void).

Matter

State +1 particles. Conventional matter as opposed to antimatter.

Master Quadratic

The equation x² - 16(G)²x + 16(G)³ = 0 whose roots give α (larger) and N_c (smaller). The central derivation mechanism.

Mass Spectrometer

Instrument measuring particle mass-to-charge ratio. Used for identifying isotopes and molecules.

Meson

Particle made of quark-antiquark pair. Examples: pion, kaon.

Meta-sLoop

An sLoop that includes a model of the sLoop itself. The defining structure of consciousness. A self-model φ(Ω) that contains φ²(φ(Ω)).

Moore Neighborhood

26 adjacent cells in 3D (all cells sharing at least one corner with center).

MUSE (MUon proton Scattering Experiment)

Experiment at PSI designed to resolve the proton radius puzzle by measuring electron and muon scattering simultaneously under identical kinematic conditions. Uses mixed lepton beams, GEM detectors, wire chambers, and scintillators to compare cross sections and form factors directly.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.15 N

N_eff (Effective Dimension)

Framework integer = 13 (Fibonacci F₇). Appears in mass formulas and the Higgs derivation.

Noetic Mass (M_Ω)

The “epistemic inertia” of an observer: resistance to belief change based on accumulated evidence. Defined as M_Ω = ∫ρ_Ω(x)dx where ρ_Ω is the observer’s belief density. Heavier noetic mass means more evidence required to shift beliefs. See also: Epistemic Inertia.

N_base (Base Modes)

Framework integer = 4. Number of base harmonic modes. Golden ratio φ = (1+√(N_base+1))/2.

N_c (Color Charges)

Framework integer ≈ 3.024 (derived as smaller root of master quadratic). floor(N_c) = 3 determines number of generations.

Nome (q = e^(-π))

The modular nome parameter from lemniscate geometry at j = 1728. The nome q = e^(-π) ≈ 0.0432 appears naturally in elliptic function theory for the lemniscatic curve. Its appearance in the alpha precision formula correction terms (via e^π) connects FTD to classical modular forms and Ramanujan’s work on elliptic integrals.

Neutrino

Nearly massless, uncharged lepton. Barely interacts. State 0 but distinct from void.

Neutron

Neutral baryon (udd). Stable in nucleus; decays freely in ~15 minutes.

Neutron Lifetime Puzzle

Unexplained ~10 second discrepancy between bottle method (τ ≈ 877.8 s) and beam method (τ ≈ 888.1 s) measurements of free neutron lifetime. FTD interpretation: measurement-context-dependent sLoop coupling may create different effective decay rates. Status: under active investigation at PSI, J-PARC, LANL, NIST.

Nucleosynthesis

Formation of atomic nuclei. Occurs in Big Bang (light elements) and stars (heavy elements).

Nineteen (19 = 2(b₃ + N_c) - 1)

Derived integer = 2 × 10 - 1 = 19. Appears in charm quark mass: m_c/m_e = 13 × 10 × 19 + 15 = 2485. A prime number.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.16 O

One Hundred Twenty-Seven (127 = N_eff(b₃ + N_c) - N_c)

Derived integer = 13 × 10 - 3 = 127. The index for the triangular number in bottom quark mass: m_b/m_e = T(127) + 42. A Mersenne prime (2⁷ - 1), the fourth Mersenne prime in the sequence.

One Hundred Thirty-Seven (137 ≈ 1/α)

The inverse fine structure constant = x₊ from master quadratic ≈ 137.036. A prime number. Often called “the most mysterious number in physics.” In FTD, 137 is derived from the lemniscatic constant G* via the master quadratic, accurate to 1.26 ppm.

One Hundred Eighty-Three (183 = N_eff(N_eff + 1) + 1)

Derived integer = 13 × 14 + 1 = 183. The strange quark to electron mass ratio: m_s/m_e = 183.

Observer (Ω)

In FTD, any manifested structure (s ≠ 0) capable of coupling to the flux field. Not privileged by consciousness: a rock can trigger collapse as well as a brain. The observer is defined by its configuration Ω(t), its horizon H(Ω,t), and its noetic mass M_Ω.

Orbit

Bound trajectory around massive object. Stable when forces balance.

Orbital

Spatial probability distribution for electron around nucleus. s, p, d, f shapes.

Ω(t) (Omega)

Complete configuration of an observer at tick \(t\). Includes every atom, neuron, memory, and state of the conscious system. The “soul” at one moment.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.17 P

Pair Production

Creation of matter-antimatter pair from sufficient energy. Creates entangled partners.

Phase Accumulator (τ)

Counter tracking relativistic time. Particle updates when τ ≥ 1.

Path Identity (Quantum Indistinguishability)

Mechanism by which quantum correlations arise from indistinguishable particle paths rather than entanglement. Demonstrated in 2025 Bell violation experiment (S = 2.275 ± 0.057, >4σ) without entangled particles, directly supporting FTD’s sLoop interpretation that correlations arise from shared substrate access.

Photon

Massless boson carrying electromagnetic force. In FTD, flux waves in void.

Planck Scale

Smallest meaningful scale. In FTD, 1 voxel = Planck length; 1 tick = Planck time.

Potential

Unrealized possibility. Carried by flux field. Precedes manifestation.

Potential vs Probability

The crucial distinction between Domain A and Domain B. Potential (flux) is ontic: it exists in physical space as a real field with causal power. Probability is epistemic: it exists in the space of knowledge as a distribution over possibilities. Confusing these leads to domain confusion.

Proton

Positive baryon (uud). Stable. Nucleus of hydrogen.

Proton Mass (π Formula)

The remarkably simple relation m_p/m_e = 6π⁵ = 1836.118, accurate to 0.002%. Uses only the integer 6 and π, with no framework integers or G. Suggests QCD binding energy emerges from pure circular geometry. Connected to the framework via 6π⁵ ≈ G⁷ × (1 - 1/13).

Proton Radius Puzzle

Discrepancy between proton charge radius measured via muonic hydrogen (~0.84 fm) and electronic hydrogen (~0.88 fm). FTD interpretation: the proton “radius” is intrinsically probe-dependent because different probes couple to different scales of the triad flux distribution. MUSE experiment at PSI testing this with simultaneous electron/muon scattering measurements.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.18 Q

Quark

Fundamental constituent of hadrons. Six flavors: up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom.

Quantum

Discrete unit. All physical quantities in FTD are quantized.

Quantum Spin Ice (QSI)

Exotic quantum state on pyrochlore lattice where magnetic moments exhibit liquid-like correlations and U(1) gauge structure. Distinguished from classical spin ice by emergent photon-like excitations near zero energy. Ce₂Zr₂O₇ confirmed as QSI in 2025, providing the first experimental validation of FTD’s mechanism for gauge boson emergence from discrete lattice dynamics.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.19 R

Regime Ratio (32)

The ratio k_physics/k_consciousness = 16/0.5 = 32 between the physics and consciousness parameter regimes. Appears as the denominator in d_min = (G*)²/32 and equals 2⁵ (one beyond highest Lemniscate-Alpha frequency 2⁴ = 16).

Relativity

Time dilation based on local energy/frequency. High-energy particles update less frequently.

Retarded Position

Source position at time of influence emission. Enforces causality.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.20 S

Sixteen (16 = N_base²)

The master quadratic coefficient = 4² = 16. The equation x² - 16(G)²x + 16(G)³ = 0 produces α and N_c. The value 16 is derived from the complementation principle: in a 2×2×2 minimal lattice, 24 links minus 7 constraints minus 1 normalization = 16 physical degrees of freedom. Also equals k_physics in the Mandelbrot mapping.

Seventeen (17 = N_eff + N_base)

Derived integer = 13 + 4 = 17. The multiplier in tau mass: m_τ/m_e = 17 × 207 - 42 = 3477. A prime number.

Sixty-Seven (67 = b₃(b₃ + N_c) - N_c)

Derived integer = 7 × 10 - 3 = 67. The numerator in the W boson mass formula: m_W/m_e = 67/(8α²). Equals 70 - 3, embedding both framework structure (70) and color charge (3). A prime number.

Seventy (70 = b₃(b₃ + N_c))

Derived integer = 7 × 10 = 70. A fundamental structure factor appearing in the electron mass derivation and the Heegner decomposition of the master quadratic (70 ± 67 structure). Related to 67 by 70 - 3 = 67.

Scattering Experiment

Technique probing structure by measuring deflection of incident particles. Rutherford scattering revealed atomic nucleus.

Schwarzschild Radius

Size of event horizon for non-rotating black hole. rs = 2GM/c².

Shell

Electron orbital layer. Numbered 1, 2, 3… with increasing radius.

Six Senses

The channels through which an observer perceives its horizon H(Ω,t): sight (EM flux), sound (pressure waves), touch (mechanical contact), taste (chemical close-range), smell (chemical distance), cognition (internal state, memory, inference).

Self-referential Iteration

Any process where output becomes input for the next cycle. The Mandelbrot iteration z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c is the purest mathematical example. In FTD, the sLoop phi -> phi(phi) + input has identical structure: the self-model feeds back as input to the next state.

sLoop (Self-referential Loop)

A closed causal structure where an observing system is part of the system being observed. The defining structure of FTD’s approach to measurement and consciousness. In an sLoop, the observer and observed share a common flux substrate, creating correlations that exceed classical bounds. Key to Bell violations (S ≈ 2√2). Distinguished from external observation by ontological continuity between observer and system. See also: Meta-sLoop.

Singularity

Point of infinite density. Classical concept; may be resolved by quantum gravity.

State

The fundamental property of a voxel. Values: -1 (antimatter), 0 (void), +1 (matter).

Spectroscopy

Technique analyzing matter by measuring emitted or absorbed electromagnetic radiation. Reveals atomic structure and composition.

**Strong Coupling (G*/π Formula)**

The remarkably simple relation α_s = G/(8π) = 0.1177, accurate to 0.15%. The factor 8π ≈ 25.13 explains why cruder approximations (G/25) also work. The ratio α_s/α ≈ 16 equals the physics coefficient k from the master quadratic.

Strong Force

Force binding quarks into hadrons. Yukawa-type with short range.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.21 T

Three Regimes (TRD-Mandelbrot)

The three parameter regions connecting TRD to the Mandelbrot set via c = 1/(k × G): (1) Physics regime: k=16, c=0.021, inside M, real roots; (2) Critical regime: k=k_c≈1.352, c=0.25, cardioid cusp, double root; (3) Consciousness regime: k=0.5, c=0.676, outside M, complex roots. The transformation is exact: k_c × c_cusp × G = 1.

Telescope

Instrument collecting electromagnetic radiation from distant objects. Types: optical, radio, X-ray, gamma-ray.

Tick

Discrete unit of time. One iteration of the causal loop.

Time Dilation

Slowing of updates for high-energy particles. Relativistic effect.

Triad

Stable three-particle configuration (equilateral). Forms nucleons.

Translation Protocol

The mathematical procedure for converting quantities between Domain A and Domain B. The Born rule P = |ψ|² is the canonical translation protocol in quantum mechanics. See also: Bridge Operator.

Triangular Number T(n)

Sum of integers 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2. T(10)=55 appears in proton mass; T(13)=91 encodes SM structure.

Thirty-Four Hundred Seventy-Seven (3477)

Tau/electron mass ratio = (N_eff + N_base) × 207 - 42 = 17 × 207 - 42 = 3477. Combines the muon ratio (207), the tau multiplier (17), and the bridge constant (42).

Two Hundred Seven (207 = 3 × b₃ × (b₃ + N_c) - N_c)

The muon/electron mass ratio = 3 × 7 × 10 - 3 = 207. One of the most famous mass ratios in particle physics, here derived purely from framework integers.

Two Thousand Four Hundred Eighty-Five (2485)

Charm/electron mass ratio = N_eff × (b₃ + N_c) × (2(b₃ + N_c) - 1) + N_eff + 2 = 13 × 10 × 19 + 15 = 2485.

Three Hundred Thirty-Four Thousand Nine Hundred Seventy (334970)

Top/electron mass ratio = 8170 × 41 = 334970. The product of the bottom quark ratio (8170) and the top/bottom multiplier (41 = N_eff × N_c + 2). The heaviest fermion mass, derived from four integers. Error: 0.92%.

Ten (10 = b₃ + N_c)

The universal sum = 7 + 3 = 10. Appears in virtually every mass formula: proton (T(10)=55), tau (17 × 207 - 42), charm (13 × 10 × 19), bottom (127 = 13 × 10 - 3). The fact that b₃ + N_c is so ubiquitous suggests deep structural significance.

Tunneling

Quantum phenomenon allowing particles to pass through classically forbidden barriers.

Ternary Valuation Theorem

The theorem (proved in ?sec-formal-logic) that exactly three valuation states {+1, −1, 0} are both necessary and sufficient for any system admitting distinguishability. This establishes that FTD’s ternary state space is not an arbitrary design choice but a logical necessity.

Two-Domain Framework

The FTD philosophical framework distinguishing Domain A (ontic/classical configurations) from Domain B (epistemic/probabilistic distributions). Neither domain is reducible to the other; both are necessary for complete description. The framework resolves measurement paradoxes by tracking which domain each quantity belongs to.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.22 U

Uniqueness Theorem

The proof that {7, 3, 13, 4} is the unique non-trivial solution to the Fibonacci skeleton constraints with multiple colors. Only three solutions exist: empty {1,1,1,0}, minimal {5,1,5,4}, and Standard Model {7,3,13,4}.

UUID

Unique identifier assigned to each manifested particle. Tracks identity through time.

𝕌 (Universe)

The set of all Global(t) across all time: { Global(t) : t ∈ ℤ }. Everything that has existed, exists, or will exist.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.23 V

Vacuum

State 0 (void). Not empty: carries flux. Zero-point fluctuations always present.

Void

State 0. The ground state of existence. Substrate of all potential.

Voxel

Fundamental 3D lattice cell. Smallest spatial unit. Contains state, flux, and properties.

Valuation Function (val)

The function val: E × Prop → V that assigns epistemic status to propositions, where V = {−1, 0, +1}. Value +1 means “affirmed” (proposition distinguished as holding), −1 means “negated” (distinguished as not holding), and 0 means “undetermined” (not yet distinguished). The foundation of EPL-ST. See ?sec-formal-logic.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.24 W

Wave

Propagating flux disturbance. Travels at maximum speed C through void.

Weak Force

Force causing flavor changes (transmutation). Responsible for beta decay.

Winding Number

A topological invariant counting how many times a curve wraps around a point. The Lemniscate-Alpha curve in the consciousness regime (k = 0.5) has winding number = -2 around the origin, indicating irreducible topological structure that cannot be continuously deformed away.

Weinberg Angle (θ_W)

Electroweak mixing angle. DERIVED as sin²θ_W = N_c/N_eff = 3/13 = 0.2308 (0.19% accuracy).

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.25 Y

xyztgψ(Δt)

Complete specification of one entity at one tick. Includes position (xyz), time (t), geometric constraint (g), modal constraint (ψ), and dynamics (Δt). The fundamental ontological unit.

Yukawa Potential

Form of strong force: proportional to exp(-mr)/r. Short range.

title: 74  Glossary
text:
74.26 Z

Zero-Point Energy

Minimum energy of vacuum. Even at “empty” void, fluctuations persist.

PARTICLE_CATALOG = {
    # Quarks
    'up': {'mass': 0.6, 'charge': 2/3, 'state': +1},
    'down': {'mass': 0.6, 'charge': -1/3, 'state': +1},
    'charm': {'mass': 25.0, 'charge': 2/3, 'state': +1},
    'strange': {'mass': 2.0, 'charge': -1/3, 'state': +1},
    'top': {'mass': 350.0, 'charge': 2/3, 'state': +1},
    'bottom': {'mass': 80.0, 'charge': -1/3, 'state': +1},

    # Leptons
    'electron': {'mass': 0.511, 'charge': -1, 'state': -1},
    'muon': {'mass': 2.1, 'charge': -1, 'state': -1},
    'tau': {'mass': 35.0, 'charge': -1, 'state': -1},
    'neutrino_e': {'mass': 0.001, 'charge': 0, 'state': 0},

    # Composite
    'proton': {
        'mass': 9.0,
        'charge': +1,
        'state': +1,
        'composition': ['up', 'up', 'down'],
        'geometry': 'triad'
    },
    'neutron': {
        'mass': 9.0,
        'charge': 0,
        'state': 0,
        'composition': ['up', 'down', 'down'],
        'geometry': 'triad'
    },
}

def create_particle(particle_type, position):
    template = PARTICLE_CATALOG[particle_type]
    particle = Voxel(position)
    particle.state = template['state']
    particle.mass = template['mass']
    particle.charge = template['charge']
    particle.uuid = generate_uuid()
    return particle


75.7.2 Composite Particle Factory
def create_proton(center_position):
    """Create a proton triad at given position."""
    # Equilateral triangle in xy-plane
    offset = 0.707  # sqrt(2)/2 for unit separation
    positions = [
        center_position + [0, offset, 0],      # up
        center_position + [-offset, -offset/2, 0],  # up
        center_position + [offset, -offset/2, 0],   # down
    ]

    quarks = [
        create_particle('up', positions[0]),
        create_particle('up', positions[1]),
        create_particle('down', positions[2]),
    ]

    # Lock the triad
    for q in quarks:
        q.is_locked = True

    return Proton(quarks)

def create_hydrogen(center_position):
    """Create hydrogen atom: proton + electron."""
    proton = create_proton(center_position)

    # Electron at shell radius
    electron_pos = center_position + [5, 0, 0]  # n=1 shell
    electron = create_particle('electron', electron_pos)
    electron.shell_n = 1

    return HydrogenAtom(proton, electron)

NoteCompanion Work



This section extends beyond what the core paper establishes. The resolution of the Strong CP problem follows from discrete lattice topology but is developed in companion papers.



77.2.1 The Problem
QCD allows a CP-violating term:
\[\mathcal{L}_\theta = \frac{\theta g^2}{32\pi^2} \epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} F_{\mu\nu}F_{\rho\sigma}\]
Experimentally: |θ| < 10⁻¹⁰
Why so small?


77.2.2 The FTD Solution: Topological Quantization
In FTD, the θ term corresponds to the winding number of flux configurations:
\[\theta = \frac{1}{8\pi^2} \int d^4x \, \vec{J} \cdot (\nabla \times \vec{J})\]
Claim: On a discrete lattice, θ is exactly quantized to integer multiples of 2π.
Proof:
The integral \(\int \mathbf{J} \cdot (\nabla \times \mathbf{J})\) counts the linking number of flux lines. On a discrete lattice:

Flux lines are discrete curves through voxels
Linking numbers are integers
Therefore: θ ∈ 2πℤ

But physical observables depend only on exp(iθ):
\[e^{i\theta} = e^{i \cdot 2\pi n} = 1 \quad \text{for all } n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Therefore: θ has no physical effect in FTD!


77.2.3 The Discrete Topology Argument
In continuous spacetime, θ can take any real value, and θ ≈ 0 requires fine-tuning. In the discrete lattice of FTD, θ ∈ 2πℤ is topologically quantized, so exp(iθ) = 1 always, and no fine-tuning is needed.

\[\delta J \sim \cos(m_a t - \vec{k} \cdot \vec{x})\]

\[m_a = \frac{\sqrt{m_u m_d}}{m_u + m_d} \cdot \frac{f_\pi m_\pi}{f_a}\]
From Lemniscate-Alpha:
\[f_a = \frac{M_P}{\alpha^{12}} \approx 10^{12} \text{ GeV}\]
This gives:
\[m_a \approx 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ eV}\]
Prediction: Axion-like particles with m_a ≈ 6 μeV exist as flux oscillations, detectable by experiments like ADMX.

title: 78  Information Quantification in FTD
text:
78.1.1 Definition 1.1 (State Information Density)
For a single voxel with ternary state \(s \in \{-1, 0, +1\}\), the maximum information content is:
\[I_{\text{state}} = \log_2(3) \approx 1.585 \text{ bits per voxel}\]
For a region \(R \subseteq \mathcal{L}\) with \(|R|\) voxels:
\[I_{\text{max}}(R) = |R| \cdot \log_2(3) \text{ bits}\]


78.1.2 Definition 1.2 (Actual State Information)
Given a probability distribution \(P(s)\) over states in region \(R\):
\[I_{\text{actual}}(R) = -\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}_R} P(c) \log_2 P(c)\]
The information deficit (how much the region is constrained):
\[\Delta I(R) = I_{\text{max}}(R) - I_{\text{actual}}(R) \geq 0\]
A fully random region has \(\Delta I = 0\). A fully determined region has \(\Delta I = I_{\text{max}}\).


78.1.3 Definition 1.3 (Flux Information)
The continuous flux field \(\mathbf{J}(v) \in \mathbb{R}^3\) requires discretization for finite information content. At resolution \(\epsilon\):
\[I_{\text{flux}}(R, \epsilon) = |R| \cdot 3 \cdot \log_2\left(\frac{J_{\text{max}}}{\epsilon}\right)\]
where \(J_{\text{max}}\) is the maximum flux magnitude.
Physical interpretation: The Planck scale sets a natural cutoff. Below Planck resolution, flux information is undefined.

title: 78  Information Quantification in FTD
text:
78.2 2. Information Measures

78.2.1 2.1 Shannon Entropy
For a configuration distribution \(P(c)\):
\[H[P] = -\sum_c P(c) \log_2 P(c)\]
Properties: - \(H \geq 0\) (non-negative) - \(H = 0\) iff deterministic (one configuration has \(P = 1\)) - \(H = H_{\text{max}}\) iff uniform distribution


78.2.2 2.2 Relative Entropy (Kullback-Leibler Divergence)
The information gained by updating from prior \(Q\) to posterior \(P\):
\[D_{KL}(P \| Q) = \sum_c P(c) \log_2 \frac{P(c)}{Q(c)} \geq 0\]
Interpretation: How many bits of “surprise” when reality is \(P\) but you expected \(Q\).


78.2.3 2.3 Mutual Information
The shared information between two regions \(A\) and \(B\):
\[I(A; B) = H[A] + H[B] - H[A, B]\]
Interpretation: How much knowing \(A\) tells you about \(B\).






ImportantMutual Information is Symmetric



\(I(A; B) = I(B; A)\)
Correlation is bidirectional. This is crucial for understanding sLoop: the observer-observed relationship is mutual.

78.3 3. Information Geometry of Space

78.3.1 Definition 3.1 (Local Information Density)
At voxel \(v\), the information density is:
\[\rho_I(v) = -\sum_{s \in \{-1,0,+1\}} P(s|v) \log_2 P(s|v)\]
This creates a scalar field over the lattice: an information landscape.


78.3.2 Definition 3.2 (Information Gradient)
\[\nabla I(v) = \left(\frac{\partial \rho_I}{\partial x}, \frac{\partial \rho_I}{\partial y}, \frac{\partial \rho_I}{\partial z}\right)\]
Physical meaning: Information flows from high-entropy (uncertain) to low-entropy (determined) regions during collapse.


78.3.3 Definition 3.3 (Information Current)
The rate of information flow through a surface \(\Sigma\):
\[\Phi_I = \int_\Sigma \rho_I \mathbf{v} \cdot d\mathbf{A}\]
where \(\mathbf{v}\) is the flux velocity field.


78.3.4 Theorem 3.1 (Information Conservation)
In a closed system, total information is conserved:
\[\frac{d}{dt} \int_V \rho_I \, dV = -\oint_{\partial V} \rho_I \mathbf{v} \cdot d\mathbf{A}\]
Information cannot be created or destroyed: only transferred or transformed.

78.5 5. Quantifying Priors

78.5.1 Definition 5.1 (Prior Distribution)
An sLoop’s prior is the probability distribution over configurations before observation:
\[\pi: \mathcal{C} \to [0, 1], \quad \sum_c \pi(c) = 1\]


78.5.2 Definition 5.2 (Prior Entropy)
The uncertainty before observation:
\[H_{\text{prior}} = H[\pi] = -\sum_c \pi(c) \log_2 \pi(c)\]
Maximum ignorance: Uniform prior, \(\pi(c) = 1/|\mathcal{C}|\), gives \(H_{\text{prior}} = \log_2 |\mathcal{C}|\).
Maximum knowledge: Deterministic prior, \(\pi(c_0) = 1\), gives \(H_{\text{prior}} = 0\).


78.5.3 Definition 5.3 (Prior Structure)
The prior is not uniform: it has structure encoding beliefs about reality:
\[\pi(c) = \frac{1}{Z} e^{-\beta E(c)}\]
where: - \(E(c)\) is the “implausibility” of configuration \(c\) - \(\beta\) is a confidence parameter - \(Z\) is the normalization (partition function)


78.5.4 5.1 Innate Priors (Built-in Structure)
Some priors are “hardwired” into the sLoop’s architecture:
\[\pi_{\text{innate}}(c) \propto \exp\left(-\sum_i w_i f_i(c)\right)\]
where \(f_i\) are feature detectors and \(w_i\) are innate weights.
Examples of innate priors: - Spatial continuity: nearby voxels likely have similar states - Temporal persistence: configurations change slowly - Conservation: total flux is approximately constant


78.5.5 5.2 Learned Priors (Acquired Structure)
Experience updates the prior via Bayes’ theorem:
\[\pi_{t+1}(c) = \frac{P(\text{obs}|c) \cdot \pi_t(c)}{P(\text{obs})}\]
The learning rate is the information gain per observation:
\[\Delta I_{\text{learn}} = D_{KL}(\pi_{t+1} \| \pi_t)\]

title: 78  Information Quantification in FTD

78.6 6. Quantifying Experience

78.6.1 Definition 6.1 (Experience)
An experience is a sequence of observations \((o_1, o_2, \ldots, o_T)\) that updates the sLoop’s internal state.


78.6.2 Definition 6.2 (Experiential Information)
The total information accumulated through experience:
\[I_{\text{exp}} = \sum_{t=1}^T D_{KL}(\pi_t \| \pi_{t-1})\]
This is the cumulative “surprise”: how much the sLoop’s beliefs have changed.


78.6.3 Definition 6.3 (Experience Entropy)
The entropy of the experience sequence:
\[H_{\text{exp}} = -\sum_{\mathbf{o}} P(\mathbf{o}) \log_2 P(\mathbf{o})\]
High \(H_{\text{exp}}\) means varied, unpredictable experiences. Low \(H_{\text{exp}}\) means repetitive, predictable experiences.


78.6.4 6.1 The Experience Integral
Over continuous time, experience accumulates:
\[I_{\text{exp}}(T) = \int_0^T \dot{I}(t) \, dt\]
where \(\dot{I}(t)\) is the instantaneous information rate (bits per tick).


78.6.5 6.2 Experience Compression
Not all observations are retained. The compression ratio is:
\[\eta = \frac{I_{\text{stored}}}{I_{\text{received}}}\]
Human memory has \(\eta \ll 1\): most experience is discarded, only patterns retained.

title: 78  Information Quantification in FTD
text:
78.7 7. The Prior-Experience Decomposition

78.7.1 Theorem 7.1 (Total Knowledge Decomposition)
An sLoop’s total knowledge \(K\) decomposes as:
\[K = K_{\text{prior}} + K_{\text{exp}} - K_{\text{forgotten}}\]
where: - \(K_{\text{prior}}\) = innate + inherited knowledge - \(K_{\text{exp}}\) = accumulated experiential information - \(K_{\text{forgotten}}\) = information lost to decay/overwriting


78.7.2 Definition 7.1 (Knowledge State)
The knowledge state at time \(t\) is the posterior distribution:
\[\kappa_t(c) = P(c | o_1, \ldots, o_t, \pi_0)\]
This encodes everything the sLoop “knows” about configurations.


78.7.3 Definition 7.2 (Knowledge Entropy)
\[H_{\text{knowledge}}(t) = H[\kappa_t]\]
As knowledge increases, entropy decreases (uncertainty shrinks).


78.7.4 The Fundamental Constraint
\[H_{\text{knowledge}}(t) \leq H_{\text{prior}} - I_{\text{exp}}(t) + H_{\text{noise}}(t)\]
You cannot know more than your priors plus experience, minus noise.

Current Status (2025):
In September 2025, representatives from all operating neutron lifetime experiments convened at PSI to address this puzzle. New results from LANL, NIST, J-PARC, and PSI are expected in coming years. BEAM METHOD:
  Neutron ← weak sLoop coupling → Vacuum
  Lower environmental flux density
  Effective decay rate: slightly lower
In FTD, the weak decay rate depends on flux field dynamics at the triad (neutron = udd configuration). If the effective phase space factor f varies with environmental flux density, different measurement contexts would yield different lifetimes, not due to exotic physics, but due to context-dependent substrate coupling.

This interpretation is speculative. FTD does not yet provide a quantitative calculation of the expected discrepancy. The puzzle may be resolved by improved experimental systematics rather than new physics.
